title: Consent for sedation and shoulder reduction
stem: Cubicle 11. Mr Yip, 19, fell on his outstretched, raised arm playing basketball. His right shoulder is deformed; he is neurovascularly intact. His X-ray is available. Explain the diagnosis and obtain consent for reduction under procedural sedation, and explain the follow-up.

phases.title: Consent
phases.goal: The procedure, the sedation, the risks, the aftercare.

review.text: Informing parents. Your notes suggest informing the parents. A patient aged 18 or over consents for himself; parents are involved only for under-18s.

Immobilisation. Your notes suggest 3–6 weeks in an immobiliser and avoiding abduction and external rotation. Current practice uses a sling for comfort for 1–3 weeks with early physiotherapy, and early referral to a shoulder surgeon for young, active patients (high recurrence).

notes:
Checked against the RCEM/RCoA guideline on safe sedation of adults in the ED (2012; RCEM 2019 update), ASA 2018 moderate sedation guideline, the Montgomery ruling (2015) on consent, and BESS/BOA guidance on first-time anterior shoulder dislocation.

Consent must cover the diagnosis, the proposed procedure and why, material risks (what a reasonable person would want to know, and what this patient would want to know), alternatives (including no treatment and other reduction methods — some can be reduced without sedation, e.g. Cunningham or external rotation; intra-articular lidocaine), and what happens next. Sedation risks: respiratory depression, airway obstruction, hypotension, vomiting and aspiration, allergy, rare cardiac arrest; the sedationist is separate from the person reducing; full monitoring and capnography; fasting is not required for ED sedation when urgent. Reduction risks: failure (needing GA), fracture (especially greater tuberosity or humeral neck), axillary nerve or vessel injury, recurrence.

Aged 18 or over, he consents for himself; you do not need to 'inform parents' as your notes suggest (that applies to under-18s in HK). Follow-up: post-reduction X-ray and neurovascular check, a sling for comfort (1–3 weeks), early physiotherapy; young, active patients have a high recurrence risk (up to 80–90% under 20) and should be referred to a shoulder surgeon early. Your notes suggest 3–6 weeks in an immobiliser and avoiding abduction and external rotation; current practice favours shorter immobilisation with early physio.

X-ray.r: The humeral head lies medial and inferior to the glenoid, below the coracoid: anterior (subcoracoid) dislocation. No fracture seen.
X-ray.mark: Describes anterior subcoracoid dislocation, no fracture

steps.label: Talk to Mr Yip
steps.hint: Diagnosis, the plan, sedation risks, reduction risks, alternatives, understanding, agreement.

turns.line: What's wrong with it? It's agony.
turns.lz: 我隻膊頭搞咩呀？痛到死。

opts.t: The ball of your shoulder has come out of the socket, to the front. We need to put it back. First, let's get you some pain relief.
opts.tz: 你膊頭個波甩咗出關節窩，向前甩咗。我哋要整返佢入去。首先，我哋俾啲止痛藥你先。
opts.rz: 唔該。你哋點樣整返入去？
opts.r: Thanks. How do you put it back?
opts.mark: Explains the diagnosis simply and offers analgesia

turns.line: How do you put it back?

opts.t: We give you a sedative through a drip so you're very sleepy and relaxed, then gently manoeuvre the arm back in. One doctor looks after the sedation and your breathing, another does the shoulder. Some shoulders go back without sedation using gentle techniques — we can try that first if you prefer.
opts.tz: 我哋會經吊針俾鎮靜劑，令你好眼瞓、好放鬆，然後輕輕咁將隻手郁返入去。一個醫生負責鎮靜同你嘅呼吸，另一個負責膊頭。有啲膊頭用溫和嘅手法，唔使鎮靜都可以整返入去——你想嘅話我哋可以先試。

opts.t: We pull hard until it clunks.
opts.tz: 我哋會用力拉，拉到「咔」一聲。

opts.t: It's generally very safe. It can slow your breathing, drop your blood pressure or make you vomit; we monitor you closely and can support your breathing if needed. Serious harm is very rare.
opts.tz: 一般嚟講好安全。有機會令你呼吸慢咗、血壓跌，或者嘔；我哋會密切監察，有需要可以幫你呼吸。嚴重傷害好罕見。

opts.t: It may not go back (then we'd do it in theatre), there's a small chance of a fracture or nerve injury, and it can dislocate again. Can you tell me back what we've discussed? Are you happy to go ahead?
opts.tz: 有機會整唔返入去（咁就要喺手術室做），有少少機會斷骨或者傷到神經，而且將來可能會再甩。你可唔可以講返我哋傾過啲咩？你同唔同意進行？
opts.rz: 可能唔成功、可能斷骨、可能會再甩。好，做啦。
opts.r: It might not work, might break, might happen again. Yes, go ahead.
opts.mark: Explains reduction risks, checks understanding and obtains consent

opts.t: An X-ray to check it's back, a check of the nerves, a sling for comfort for a week or two, and early physiotherapy. Because you're young and play sport, the chance of it happening again is high, so I'll refer you to the shoulder surgeons.
opts.tz: 照 X 光確定整返入去，檢查神經，用手托吊一兩個禮拜會舒服啲，然後盡早做物理治療。因為你後生又做運動，再甩嘅機會好高，所以我會轉介你去膊頭專科。
opts.mark: Explains follow-up, recurrence risk and referral
